messages:
Nina S: Quick heads-up: Orpheus-v2-ptq (int8 PTQ) was pushed into the canary pool this morning. Perf looks fine but structured toolcall parse errors spiked. canary-bot posted the run: https://ci.internal/redwood/canary/orpheus-v2

Carlos M: What magnitude? Is it parser-only or a downstream hallucination issue? :mag:

Jin (Infra): Canary telemetry: toolcall_parse_fail = 4.1% (n=950). FP16 baseline for same harness is ~0.12%. Failure buckets: trailing-text-after-json, missing-closing-brace, truncated-array-end.

Rahul: Copied anonymized failing sample from artifacts:
```
{"cmd":"call_external","params":{"q":"deploy guide"},"meta":{"ver":2}}
Additional notes: try the new flag in CLI.
```
The object finishes cleanly then the model appends a casual sentence on the next token  breaks strict parsers.

Nina S: I can reproduce locally with streaming enabled + kv-cache ON, batch=12. Disabling kv-cache or increasing chunk_size reduces suffix noise. Hypothesis: quantized output tokenization + streaming chunk boundaries cause punctuation/token off-by-one leading to trailing free-text.

Carlos M: Short-term: implement a non-blocking rescue in serving (greedy-last-brace + strip-after) to avoid immediate user-facing breakage. Long-term: run a quant/bpe alignment sweep.

Jin (Infra): I've exported top-300 failing prompts into eval harness (erun-57432C). Plan: run them across fp16, ptq-int8(per-tensor), ptq-int8(per-channel), ptq-int8(sym/asym) and variants with kv-cache off. Also add a streaming-slice test that chops outputs into 24-token frames to reproduce chunked delivery.

canary-bot: Canary summary: model=Orpheus-v2-ptq(int8), samples=950, parse_fail=4.1%, mean_rt=158ms, link=https://ci.internal/redwood/canary/orpheus-v2/results

Rahul: Note: some rejects are valid JSON but fail our strict key-order check. We should be careful about relaxing checks since that erodes signal.

Nina S: Agreed keep strictness for signal. Proposed two-stage flow: (1) non-blocking repair attempt in serving (try-find-last-balanced-brace, drop trailing garbage, json.loads check); if repaired mark as rescued metadata; (2) keep original failure counts visible so we don't hide regressions.

Carlos M: I'll open an opt-in per-canary PR for the rescue filter and ensure both original and repaired payloads are logged for analysis.

Jin (Infra): Action items: @Jin -> run eval matrix + streaming-slice by EOD; @Carlos -> PR for rescue filter + telemetry tagging; @Rahul -> histogram of failure categories + top offending prompts. I'll coordinate quant-bisect (per-tensor vs per-channel, sym vs asym) and share results tomorrow AM.

Nina S: Decision: hold broader rollout until either parse_fail < 0.5% across canary matrix OR rescue + telemetry is in place and ops signs off. Thanks all :thumbsup:
